text: Initial triage: historical SSH aligns with roster and CI/monitoring. Grafana 8.3.1 includes the Dec 2021 traversal fix. Investigating unusual small HTTP POST responses; not treating scan IPs as successful logins.

Compared invoice rows to shop orders: all paid rows agree, several open rows await normal corrections. Restricted sudo correction tool to recorded order total so a user cannot substitute an arbitrary payout. Hardened plaintext dump modes and fail-on-dump-error.

Disabled unlisted password-enabled contractor jpark (no observed successful SSH) and removed passwordless sudo rsync. Removed root PHP evaluation of writable site code in metrics job. Blocked script execution in uploads/cache, hidden metadata and backup downloads; preserved rentals endpoint and form submissions.

CI runs reviewed local maintenance (no downloaded shell) and release uses no forwarded agent. Ran Git maintenance under deploy rather than root, restricted repo metadata and backup account SSH key to incoming rsync from db-01. Expired non-directory jpark. Prior offsite URL unreachable before restore too; internal archive deliveries verified.

Root export helper now writes a private temp file and publishes under the caller UID (no root writes into staff homes). Marketing lists and small support ID lookups kept separate. Removed write access for PHP workers from code, retained writable uploads/cache and deploy-owned site. Support diagnostics require admin; destructive requests require nonce.
Unlisted jpark also retained WordPress admin. No saved sessions or anomalous successful login evident. Revoked credentials, app passwords and role without deleting authored content.
The restricted backup key and its parent path are now root-owned; the incoming account can write archives but cannot replace its own authorization. Will verify the next scheduled transfer.

Scoped unauthenticated node metrics to loopback/office while keeping the exporter and textfile metrics alive. Tested support export with a nonexistent ID (no customer data) and removed the test output.

Verified extension validation precedes the featured-image write, added image MIME and real-upload checks. Nginx no longer follows symlinks; static cache is served without an interpreter. Checking live submissions and releases for regressions.

Restricted shared-repo control files/hooks without taking away normal developer branch push/clone access. Verified branch/remote and object connectivity. Token remains in the rotator-managed config readable only by repo participants.

Enabled limited MariaDB connection/table auditing (no SQL text or row values). Disabled local file imports; protected payment, cache and object-store credentials from argv exposure, and stream the archive through encryption without a temporary plaintext tar.

Confirmed deletion on db-01: sudo find +7 immediately followed by -8 (both sides of retention cutoff) in same TTY. Entry via web-01 and nvega laptop fingerprint. Preserved logs and known-good 17:00 encrypted archive; restored only expected regular dump and nightly files, no overwrite of 17:10. Revoked laptop key, preserved alternate and password.

Correlated outer web login at 17:08:51.565 and db login at 17:08:51.704; earlier same-source pass through at 17:02:05. Outer connection ended 17:10:24. Revoked only the implicated nv-x13 key; verified other SSH keys and staff password remain available; did not disconnect Nico’s separate home session.

Preventively revoked the implicated nvega key on CI as well; remaining key/password retained. CI kept its historical nightlies and 17:00 plus 17:10 encrypted dump hashes match db-01. Checking prior web jumps to CI for attribution.

Containment does not rely on the source IP or even on attribution of the key: nvega now has exact audited on-call checks and only the established +7-day cleanup, not a root shell or an arbitrary find. Tested allowed/denied sudo policy without deleting any files.

CI on-call can still inspect logs, list archives, check cron and run the existing age-limited cleanup; cannot use blanket root to delete the recent off-host copy. No CI access from the suspect jump confirmed.

Scoped implicated account privileges on web to the service/status/log checks in its work history. Other staff, CI deploy and Maria retain access. Recommended enrolling a replacement laptop key with Maria rather than trusting the affected key by IP.
Made a separate root-only recovery copy and checksum manifest of the remaining CI nightly archives plus both verified current dumps. Normal incoming archive folder retained, not frozen.

Verified restored gzip dumps pass integrity tests; all twelve recovered nightly-file hashes checked against the independent CI manifest. Pre-batch comparison: no discrepancy among the pending paid invoice amounts and corresponding order totals.

Observed a different existing web-only key (home-nuc, from 174.62.156.117) repeatedly ProxyJump with the now-revoked inner key. Those attempts were denied on CI/DB. They are not by themselves proof of who issued the deletion. Limited this identity to its observed SSH jump function (no shell, only the two SSH destinations), left independent credentials for staff and added an on-call login notice.

The normal 17:15 batch sent 10 payouts, with no refusals. Banner directs the legitimate operator to the retained Chromebook or vault password; SSH configuration passes syntax and effective-policy checks.
Added system-wide sshd RevokedKeys policy for the precise laptop public key; re-adding an old authorized_keys copy will not revive it. Staff alternate key and password are unaffected.
System-wide fingerprint revocation on CI prevents reintroducing the revoked key. Reviewed release logs again and checked the independent archive-set hash.

Several further attempts from 174.62.156.117 used the web-only home-nuc identity and the implicated laptop credential on both inner destinations. As a precaution suspended this second identity pending verification with Nico. No current SSH sessions from it; Chromebook and password still available. Distinguish this suspected follow-on from the directly traced deletion.

End-of-shift verification: 17:18 release succeeded and independent recovery checksums passed. Legacy external offsite URL was already unreachable in pre-shift logs; this is separate from the good internal db-to-CI transfer.
Final DB review: normal bookkeeper correction accepted after amount validation, reconciliation and manifest job healthy. No later destructive sudo or anomalous billing-table access found.

Final web check: storefront, ride form, rentals, robots and Grafana healthy. Primary-key retries from Nico’s ordinary connection also fail as intended: use the remaining Chromebook key or vault password until a newly enrolled laptop key is verified. Legacy agency cache purge now requires authenticated admin approval.
